idh.reasoning: The metadata favors an IDH-mutant diffuse glioma because the patient is young by adult glioma standards on age_years, and the lesion is predominantly temporal-cortical with cortical involvement on Tumor Location, Region Proportions, and Cortical involvement, a pattern more often seen with lower-grade/IDH-mutant diffuse glioma than primary IDH-wildtype glioblastoma. Mild and very small-volume enhancement on Enhancement Quality, ET Volume (mL), and Proportion Enhancing also supports IDH-mutant disease over a typical intensely enhancing IDH-wildtype glioblastoma. Features arguing against IDH-mutant status include substantial edema and mass effect on ED Volume (mL), Proportion of Oedema, midline_shift_present, and max_shift_mm, plus a reported necrotic/nonenhancing component and thick enhancing margin on Proportion Necrosis and Thickness of enhancing margin, which can be seen with aggressive IDH-wildtype glioblastoma. Overall, the young age and cortical temporal phenotype with only minimal enhancement outweigh the aggressive mass-effect features, so the best estimate is IDH-mutant.

overall_comment: Predictions are based only on structured conventional MRI metadata without DWI/ADC, perfusion, spectroscopy, SWI/GRE, or calcification assessment. The very small enhancing volume but reported high necrotic/nonenhancing proportion creates uncertainty for WHO grade. Molecular testing remains required for definitive WHO CNS5 classification.

The strongest grade-4-supporting metadata are a large reported necrotic/nonenhancing component on Proportion Necrosis and NCR Volume (mL), thick enhancing margin on Thickness of enhancing margin, extensive edema on ED Volume (mL) and Proportion of Oedema, and substantial mass effect on midline_shift_present, mean_shift_mm, max_shift_mm, p95_shift_mm, Asymmetrical Ventricles, and Effaced Ventricle. Large Total tumor volume (mL) also supports high-grade behavior. Features arguing against grade 4 include only mild and tiny enhancing tumor burden on Enhancement Quality, ET Volume (mL), and Proportion Enhancing, younger age on age_years, and no ependymal or deep white matter invasion on Ependymal (ventricular) Invasion and Deep WM invasion. On balance, the necrotic/nonenhancing burden plus edema and mass effect outweigh the minimal enhancement, so grade 4 is the best estimate, but confidence is limited by the small enhancing volume and lack of advanced sequences.
